scenes.headline: What an agent's cost per task is made of
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Smolder! Meta says its new small model does a task for a third of what a rival charges. Let's open the bill.

scenes.text: When three models charge the same per token, a cheaper task means fewer tokens, or a cheaper price for the tokens an agent re-sends.
scenes.say: When three models charge the same per token, a cheaper task means fewer tokens, or a cheaper price for tokens sent again and again.

steps.say: A bigger model plans, and hands the repeated small jobs to Ember.
Ember calls a tool, runs a test, or updates a record.
The result joins the conversation, and the whole conversation is sent again on the next turn.
Most of it was sent before, so it comes from the cache. In the benchmark run, ninety-eight percent of Ember's input did.

scenes.title: Cost of one task, per million tokens
scenes.text: cost = out x 0.50 + cached x 0.004 + new x 0.10
scenes.say: So the bill for one task has three terms.

parts.note: output tokens, same price for all three models
parts.say: Output tokens cost the same for all three models. Ember simply writes fewer of them.

parts.note: Ember's cache price; the rivals pay 0.01
parts.say: Cached input is the one price that differs. Ember's is less than half its rivals'.

parts.note: fresh input, a small share in an agent
parts.say: Fresh input is a small share once the cache is warm.

scenes.title: Output tokens per index task
scenes.say: At max effort Ember writes about as much as Haiku at high effort, and scores higher. Haiku at max writes nearly three times as much.

scenes.label: Ember's cost as a share of Haiku's, before and after equal cache prices
scenes.note: Artificial Analysis cost per task, max effort
scenes.say: The third holds. Price Ember's cache like Haiku's and it becomes a bit over half. Two thirds of the saving is tokens.

scenes.credit: Meta's Muse Ember post on X
scenes.title: Meta's results table

steps.note: AutomationBench: a lead well beyond noise
steps.say: In Meta's table, the clearest lead is AutomationBench, business workflows through app interfaces. With six hundred and fifty seven tasks, it is beyond the noise.

scenes.text: With equal token prices, compare tokens per task and the cache price, not the headline ratio.
scenes.say: With equal token prices, compare tokens per task and the cache price, not the headline ratio.

recap: A cheaper cache does a third
scenes.say: Same token prices, fewer tokens. A cheaper cache does a third. And keep each context under two hundred thousand tokens.
